# Application call comparison — read-only evidence

Examined TaxKit `f899c963f463d2283517e908febcfa3ebb1dd442` on clean `codex/common-practice-foundation-review`, and Common Practice `54a62a5d64892ee2304260f51ef683fb299deea7` on clean `main`. No app, package or Common Practice files changed. Parent owns the frozen install and current local checks. Dependency-source observations made before that install saw TaxKit Alchemy beta.79; do not treat those as the final installed graph. Published scaffold 0.6.11 was checked by the parent against manifest and release after my public lookup failed.

## Shape and recommended reuse order

```text
Website HTML / React forms      machine HTTP / RPC / MCP
          |                               |
          +---- checked transport --------+
                           |
                   native API Worker
                           |
                PublicCalculatorService
                           |
             catalogue -> Core engine -> AU rules
                           |
                checked report + diagnostics

local TypeScript SDK --------> same calculator service
```

Reuse the Common Practice native Website/API connection and single server runner as the app base; reuse its named client operations and closed errors; retain TaxKit's calculator/core/rules/SDK owners; preserve wire routes and exports with compatibility adapters; then qualify any replacement of the private calculation connection before retiring its current code. HTTP versus RPC for the Website is a design decision after this comparison, not an already settled correction.

## Concrete Website HTTP versus RPC comparison

| Concern | Common Practice / scaffold | Current TaxKit | Recommendation and consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Website server reads | Common Practice `ApiClientsLive` builds typed HTTP Content and Training clients over the native private binding (`apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts:70-90`). Scaffold uses `fromCloudflareFetcher` and `toHttpClient` then named domain client Layer (`repo-structure/assets/repository/apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts.tmpl:29-51`). | `WebsiteServerLive` builds calculator and docs RPC clients over matching private binding (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:33-208`). | HTTP can be the shared default base. Keeping RPC is also valid if the richer contracts and current proof justify it. Neither choice requires changing a tax rule. |
| Browser calls | Common Practice's browser WebMCP calls typed HTTP Content/Training services through checked API settings (`apps/web/src/lib/runtime.client.ts:88-124`). Normal page loading uses TanStack server functions (`apps/web/src/lib/seo/page.functions.ts:13-29`). | React Atom owns calculator RPC calls to public POST `/rpc` (`apps/web/src/lib/calculator.atoms.ts:37-89`). Root checks and seeds configuration (`apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:49-91`). Docs use server functions instead of an independent browser backend. | Prefer one closed Website client contract independent of transport; either private HTTP/public HTTP or private RPC/public RPC may implement it. Keep direct public API calculation and same page-owned command state. |
| Private rate identity | Common Practice has content reads, no equivalent anonymous-tax calculation allowance in the inspected path. | TaxKit refuses forwarded Worker IP headers and sends the checked original connection identity through a private Worker method, separate from JSON (`packages/api/rpc/src/rate-identity.boundary.ts:11-20`; `apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:213-239`). | Necessary preservation. Plain binding fetch must not replace this method until it has an equally trusted identity path. A new checked HTTP client alone does not solve this. |
| Private cancellation | Native binding HTTP can carry an operation signal. Common Practice server entry forwards the request signal (`apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts:93-101`). | Calculator private `toRpcAsync` call explicitly cannot carry AbortSignal; local cancellation stops waiting, while server work remains bounded (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:60-73`). Docs byte-body binding fetch supplies a signal (`:174-180`). | HTTP has a simpler cancellable transport, but trusted identity and actual remote abort must both be proved. Keep the present limit stated until replacement proof exists. |
| Client service | Common Practice HTTP and RPC Layers implement the same Content service; generated native client is private (`packages/http/src/client.layer.ts:25-64`; `packages/rpc/src/client.layer.ts:28-56`). | RPC has a checked named transport client (`packages/api/rpc/src/service.ts:22-54`). HTTP exposes the generated client and callback wrapper (`packages/api/http/src/client/index.ts:12-24`; `client/service.ts:5-17`). | Important correction: add named checked HTTP operations and keep old entrypoints as compatibility adapters. Do not simply widen the local SDK's error contract to transport errors. |
| Errors | Common Practice maps unavailable/invalid replies to Content-owned errors, retaining semantic failures (`packages/http/src/client.layer.ts:15-60`). | RPC projects private request failures to `CalculatorRpcRejected`, retains canonical capacity/rate/time errors, and adds transport errors (`handlers.ts:15-65`; `errors.ts:16-100`). HTTP generated client exposes HTTP/Schema errors and HTTP envelopes. | A checked Website-facing service should share safe named failures regardless of transport, while HTTP status/error bytes and RPC revision 4 stay unchanged. |
| Whole reply limits | Common Practice HTTP timeout wraps the complete native client operation (40 seconds due image rendering; `packages/http/src/client.layer.ts:31-59`, `content/src/service.ts:15-16`). | RPC is ten seconds including reply decode and cleanup, 2 MiB body cap, no automatic retry (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:55-85`; `response-budget.boundary.ts:12-53`; `schemas.ts:60-61`). HTTP helper has no owning complete-read deadline or byte budget (`client/index.ts:12-16`). | Important correction: supply full-read deadline, byte cap, invalid-reply failure and earlier caller cancellation for the new HTTP client. Keep TaxKit's ten-second budget; Common Practice's 40-second image budget does not fit tax calculation. |
| RPC receive loop lifetime | Common Practice RPC client is acquired once (`packages/rpc/src/client.layer.ts:27-31`); it is not the Website's chosen transport. | TaxKit creates/releases each native RPC client in the named operation; retaining an earlier Worker request's receive loop can stall later requests (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:87-107`). | Preserve TaxKit's scope while RPC remains. Copying Common Practice's once-acquired RPC client into this Website would undo a deliberate request-lifetime fix. |
| Documentation reach | Common Practice HTTP Content has selected data/Markdown/SEO/image variants. | TaxKit RPC also has named discovery, navigation, page, search and Markdown operations. Public HTTP currently has four content routes; discovery uses the private RPC operation (`packages/api/http/README.md:43-46`; `apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:145-150`). | HTTP-only Website needs a checked replacement for discovery too. Do not invent a second documentation renderer or source loader in Website. |
| SDK | Common Practice packages are private source-only. | TaxKit SDK is in-process, not a network client (`packages/sdk/typescript/package.json:4-5`; `src/effect.ts:91-117`; `live.layer.ts:1-9`). | Keep SDK contract, caller-owned lifetime, engine calculation and dist-only exports regardless of Website transport. A Website change has no reason to turn this into a remote SDK. |

Recommendation for the later transport round: use typed HTTP as the default app-base path once the named safe HTTP client and trusted private rate identity are qualified; retain public RPC for existing machine consumers. The alternative is to keep RPC for the Website, preserving its already explicit timeout/byte/cancellation/error policy, while still fixing the weaker HTTP client. This is optional simplification, not evidence that RPC calculations are wrong.

## Representative traces with exact owners

1. Browser calculation: page container wires one Atom command and interrupts it on unmount (`apps/web/src/lib/calculator-page.container.tsx:65-85`). Atom runtime acquires matching public RPC transport (`calculator.atoms.ts:47-89`). Editing interrupts pending work and keeps a stale report (`:98-148`, `:168-225`). RPC encodes `Calculate` revision 4 with native Schemas, scopes its receive loop, disables tracing, enforces ten-second completion and maps fixed failures (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:55-107`). API routes use the same `PublicCalculatorService` (`apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:87-117`; RPC handlers `packages/api/rpc/src/handlers.ts:46-65`). Calculator owner selects entry and maps input failures (`packages/calculators/src/live.layer.ts:34-66,83-94`). The entry decodes its actual facts once (`catalog.ts:110-121`) then supplies the scenario + AU rule Layer to Core (`:142-153` for take-home; `:207-217` for annual). Core provides that rule/scenario Layer and returns report + diagnostics (`packages/core/src/engine/live.layer.ts:11-21`). RPC encodes the checked response, Atom receives it, leaf renders readonly report.

2. HTML form without JavaScript: Website admits and bounds form POST, checks form data, constructs the owning request and calls `WebsiteServerApplication.calculate` (`apps/web/src/server.ts:177-237`). Private adapter sends native `/rpc` Request plus original checked identity to API binding-only `calculatorRequest` (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:53-92`; `apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:213-239`). API buffers/bounds the JSON reply before the native method's event scope closes (`:241-275`). Website Schema-encodes success/failure into plain TanStack submission data (`server.ts:234-251`), root restores checked result, the page keeps no independent backend. Only plain report/form values enter request context. Changing this custom entry needs no-JavaScript, safe failure and response-consumption proof; it should not be removed just because Common Practice has no tax form.

3. Remote HTTP calculation: native route group decodes URL/body/query with calculator-owned Schemas and preserves existing HTTP error/status envelopes (`packages/api/http/src/groups/calculators.ts:62-104`; handlers `:83-120`). The handler calls the same service; SDK is not in the server dependency path. Request body owner admits streamed 64 KiB within five seconds (`packages/api/http/src/request-boundary.ts:33-83`). API composition shares the calculation service instance across HTTP and RPC. HTTP client generation uses the same API declarations, but its public helper currently leaves timeout and transport-failure ownership to each consumer.

4. Local SDK: caller-selected descriptor supplies calculator identity and input/report types; canonical context/query constructors precede calculator service call and selected report validation (`packages/sdk/typescript/src/effect.ts:71-117`). Default Layer supplies the same calculator service + Core engine (`live.layer.ts:1-9`). Plain clients have independent lazily started ManagedRuntime, stop pending work when closed, await cleanup; one-shot helpers own temporary Scope (`client.runtime.ts:66-75,95-173,177-225`). Effect callers keep their own service provision and lifetime. This is justified machinery for a Promise SDK, not a duplicate server runner.

5. Remote MCP: six app-owned toolkit definitions reuse canonical calculator/content inputs and replies (`apps/api/src/mcp.tools.layer.ts:24-90`). `taxkit_calculate` calls the captured calculator service and projects failures to fixed tool guidance (`:92-148`). The tool has explicit request cancellation that removes its AbortSignal listener and waits for losing work cleanup (`mcp-cancellation.boundary.ts:6-39`). Native API instance composes modern `2026-07-28` once; registration removes first caller's request/key/signal from retained context (`worker.application.ts:121-157`). Legacy `2025-11-25` sessions have a stage-owned Durable Object, ten-minute Scope with 32 initialisations/32 concurrent requests, native alarm expiry (`mcp-session.layer.ts:51-147`; `mcp.schemas.ts:4-8`). Reply JSON/SSE is fully read under request Scope, 2 MiB/ten seconds, no subscriptions/resumption (`mcp-response.boundary.ts:11-49`). Current documented modern real-network pre-response cancellation relies on the five-second work budget; do not describe in-process early interruption as remote cleanup proof (`docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md:720-727`).

## Findings for root crosswalk (provisional IDs)

- APP-001 — important — HTTP client is a raw generated client rather than named checked operations. Earliest owner `packages/api/http/src/client/*`, owner `taxkit-http-api-owner`. Consequence: HTTP consumers repeat deadline/error/credential/redirect/byte policy; the Website cannot simply substitute it for the checked RPC client. Correction: narrow named service backed by private native client; explicit typed origin, fixed failures, whole-read budget and capped reply. Keep existing client creation methods, callback helper and export paths as compatibility adapters until separately approved retirement. Tests: native HTTP good/declared error/malformed body/wrong selected reply/stalled headers then body/caller interruption/secret-negative error. Rollback: leave legacy client path and switch Website imports back; no tax/wire alteration.
- APP-002 — optional simplification — Website private transport has two handwritten HttpClient adapters and binding-only calculatorRequest, and raw Request/Response materialisation (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:53-116,165-204`). Earliest owner Website private binding adapter; backend private method/rate owner. Consequence: extra request-body and cancellation code has to stay qualified on Alchemy updates. Correction: adopt the shared native bridge as far as actual host identity, byte-body and abort semantics allow; preserve trusted rate identity and test multiple sequential Worker requests after startup. Retirement conditional: existing docs byte-body custom adapter, custom private HttpClient construction, and private calculatorRequest buffer can only be retired after equivalent identity/cancellation/lifetime proof. HTTP versus RPC is a later choice.
- APP-003 — preserve justified difference — RPC has separate safe client contract and request/procedure/response policy. Merging it directly into PublicCalculatorService would expose different failures or change SDK expectations. Keep transport projection and domain tax owner separate. A safe consumer-facing contract may be shared within existing calculator owner, but changing public error unions is a declared compatibility change, not a folder rename.
- APP-004 — preserve necessary difference — TaxKit needs compiled dist-only packages/SDK rather than Common Practice source-only manifests. `packages/sdk/typescript/package.json:14-38` and packed/downstream scripts are the owners. Common Practice Content/HTTP/RPC/MCP `package.json` directly resolve `src`; those are useful private-app patterns but do not prove TaxKit tarball compatibility. Removing source/types/default/publish maps, changing package names or moving exports is breaking unless old names continue to resolve. Keep source condition for local internal packages and dist-only actual publish staging; retain packed installed consumer, declaration and browser bundle proof.
- APP-005 — preserve necessary difference — tax request limits, anonymous rate identity, shared work pool and safe logging. `packages/calculators/src/work.layer.ts:9-56` gives each composed isolate eight places/five seconds. Timer cannot stop synchronous CPU; late result is rejected (`:25-33`). No global pool is claimed. Do not copy Common Practice wildcard browser CORS (`apps/api/src/http/handler.layer.ts:46-61`) to the tax API. TaxKit admits exact Website origin and disables native client tracing as containment (`apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:189-204`; RPC live `:68`, server `packages/api/rpc/src/server.ts:10-15`). Operational tracing requires reviewed safe fields, actual browser b3/traceparent preflight and errors, rather than changing CORS alone.
- APP-006 — optional — move app-owned MCP tool contracts into a package only if there is a real second consumer. Common Practice's shared ContentToolHandlers works for remote MCP and browser tools (`packages/mcp/src/handlers.layer.ts:6-16`). TaxKit browser tools deliberately operate the page's existing form/answer state; a plain remote calculate handler is not the same interaction. Preserve UI command coordination. Legacy Durable Object session/expiry stays API-host owned regardless of contract location.
- APP-007 — agreed preservation after Q2 — both Bun and Cloudflare remain supported. Native API Worker has HTTP/RPC/MCP with rate policy; Bun host currently serves retained HTTP composition only (`apps/api/src/server.ts:1-28`, `src/index.ts:1-20`, `package.json` dev/start). Preserve Bun launcher and adapter. Do not present Bun `dev` as native-pair proof. Each host requires its own proved request/response/cancellation adapter; shared package code and calculation/report contracts remain host-independent. No need to copy native Cloudflare-only rate binding into Bun.
- APP-008 — important ownership correction for agreed host independence — Cloudflare edge identity extraction is inside RPC package `packages/api/rpc/src/rate-identity.boundary.ts:11-20` (reads `cf-worker`/`cf-connecting-ip` and trusts only direct edge ingress), though it serves all native transports. Move the actual edge trust decision into an app-owned Cloudflare ingress adapter; keep calculator-owned `CalculatorClientRateKey`/`CalculatorRequestRateKey`/`CalculatorAdmission` contracts (`packages/calculators/src/admission.service.ts:10-26`) host-neutral. Preserve old private RPC export as a re-export if current callers need it until imports move. No removal of the trusted private Website calculation method is implied. `apps/api/src/worker-admission.layer.ts:6-59` correctly owns native Alchemy RateLimit construction and adapts it into the calculator interface. `packages/api/rpc/src/host-telemetry.ts:1-27` imports only Effect and is not a Cloudflare runtime coupling; its naming/placement can be reviewed with observability ownership, but do not invent a provider-import violation.

## Shared composition for the agreed Bun and Cloudflare hosts

Direct source search found no imports of Alchemy, `cloudflare:workers`, `@effect/platform-bun`, `@effect/platform-node`, Bun/Node built-ins or ambient `process`, and no `Effect.run*`/ManagedRuntime in current calculator/Core/HTTP/RPC source. The two observed Worker mentions in RPC are explanatory comments, except the concrete edge-header policy listed in APP-008. SDK's private Promise bridge is deliberately an execution boundary; it is not a domain service runner.

Recommended shared composition remains in the API app: one host-neutral route/application Layer merges HTTP and RPC handler Layers using the supplied calculator/content services; native Worker and Bun adapters each acquire that graph once under their host lifetime, supply their own request/cancellation/response services, and close each request's work. Calculator package owns the reusable eight-place/five-second work decoration, input/output Schemas and tax dispatch. Provider-specific identity and rate-binding adapters stay outside packages. Bun's existing lack of Cloudflare rate admission should remain explicit unless a separately agreed Bun admission policy is added. The Website stays a separate client-only app. Native Worker continues its incoming Effect execution; Bun uses `HttpRouter.serve` and one top-level `BunRuntime.runMain`; shared service/domain code never runs a Promise or builds a second ManagedRuntime.

The initial common route composition can cover current HTTP contract and RPC together without changing tax calculations. Whether Bun gains RPC/MCP host support is a separate supported-surface decision: preserving both hosts does not itself promise a Cloudflare Durable Object equivalent on Bun. Legacy MCP protocol/session policy remains a host adapter concern; checked tool definitions and handlers may be reused. Validate local host behaviour independently, then compare decoded reports/errors against the same calculator test Layer. Rollback keeps current `ApiAppLayer` and native `ApiWorkerApplication` exports as adapters until their caller inventory and proofs are complete.

## Local validation limits

I ran two checks before the parent's frozen install. `bun run --filter=@taxkit/api-rpc test` exited 1: four suites, zero tests; missing workspace exports (`@taxkit/content/live`, `/errors`) and undefined Schema union member. `bun run --filter=api test` exited 1: script could not find Vitest. These are unqualified stale installation/build observations, not proved source failures. Parent subsequently froze installed graph and owns builds/current validation. No further tests run here. Existing test sources are strong required checks but reading them is not executing them:

- RPC `test/deadline.test.ts:34-76,77-109` checks stalled header/body whole deadline and earlier caller interruption.
- Native Website pair `apps/web/test/native-pair.boundary.test.ts:179-229` checks actual built browser lacks engine/provider/server implementation markers, with positive API marker check.
- Native browser cancellation `native-cancellation.boundary.test.ts:403-405` explicitly caps remote-operation claims.
- API official MCP client `apps/api/test/mcp-client.boundary.test.ts:241-352` tests actual client cancellation and calculation-place release.
- SDK lifetime `packages/sdk/typescript/src/client-lifetime.test.ts` covers separate clients, pending startup/work, close race and private defects; packed/downstream scripts own real package proof.

No tax correctness, final current local test pass, hosted deployment, provider state or published package claim is made by this note.

Local SDK: caller-selected descriptor supplies calculator identity and input/report types; canonical context/query constructors precede calculator service call and selected report validation (`packages/sdk/typescript/src/effect.ts:71-117`). Default Layer supplies the same calculator service + Core engine (`live.layer.ts:1-9`). Plain clients have independent lazily started ManagedRuntime, stop pending work when closed, await cleanup; one-shot helpers own temporary Scope (`client.runtime.ts:66-75,95-173,177-225`). Effect callers keep their own service provision and lifetime. This is justified machinery for a Promise SDK, not a duplicate server runner.

5. Remote MCP: six app-owned toolkit definitions reuse canonical calculator/content inputs and replies (`apps/api/src/mcp.tools.layer.ts:24-90`). `taxkit_calculate` calls the captured calculator service and projects failures to fixed tool guidance (`:92-148`). The tool has explicit request cancellation that removes its AbortSignal listener and waits for losing work cleanup (`mcp-cancellation.boundary.ts:6-39`). Native API instance composes modern `2026-07-28` once; registration removes first caller's request/key/signal from retained context (`worker.application.ts:121-157`). Legacy `2025-11-25` sessions have a stage-owned Durable Object, ten-minute Scope with 32 initialisations/32 concurrent requests, native alarm expiry (`mcp-session.layer.ts:51-147`; `mcp.schemas.ts:4-8`). Reply JSON/SSE is fully read under request Scope, 2 MiB/ten seconds, no subscriptions/resumption (`mcp-response.boundary.ts:11-49`). Current documented modern real-network pre-response cancellation relies on the five-second work budget; do not describe in-process early interruption as remote cleanup proof (`docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md:720-727`).

## Findings for root crosswalk (provisional IDs)

- APP-001 — important — HTTP client is a raw generated client rather than named checked operations. Earliest owner `packages/api/http/src/client/*`, owner `taxkit-http-api-owner`. Consequence: HTTP consumers repeat deadline/error/credential/redirect/byte policy; the Website cannot simply substitute it for the checked RPC client. Correction: narrow named service backed by private native client; explicit typed origin, fixed failures, whole-read budget and capped reply. Keep existing client creation methods, callback helper and export paths as compatibility adapters until separately approved retirement. Tests: native HTTP good/declared error/malformed body/wrong selected reply/stalled headers then body/caller interruption/secret-negative error. Rollback: leave legacy client path and switch Website imports back; no tax/wire alteration.
- APP-002 — optional simplification — Website private transport has two handwritten HttpClient adapters and binding-only calculatorRequest, and raw Request/Response materialisation (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:53-116,165-204`). Earliest owner Website private binding adapter; backend private method/rate owner. Consequence: extra request-body and cancellation code has to stay qualified on Alchemy updates. Correction: adopt the shared native bridge as far as actual host identity, byte-body and abort semantics allow; preserve trusted rate identity and test multiple sequential Worker requests after startup. Retirement conditional: existing docs byte-body custom adapter, custom private HttpClient construction, and private calculatorRequest buffer can only be retired after equivalent identity/cancellation/lifetime proof. HTTP versus RPC is a later choice.
- APP-003 — preserve justified difference — RPC has separate safe client contract and request/procedure/response policy. Merging it directly into PublicCalculatorService would expose different failures or change SDK expectations. Keep transport projection and domain tax owner separate. A safe consumer-facing contract may be shared within existing calculator owner, but changing public error unions is a declared compatibility change, not a folder rename.
- APP-004 — preserve necessary difference — TaxKit needs compiled dist-only packages/SDK rather than Common Practice source-only manifests. `packages/sdk/typescript/package.json:14-38` and packed/downstream scripts are the owners. Common Practice Content/HTTP/RPC/MCP `package.json` directly resolve `src`; those are useful private-app patterns but do not prove TaxKit tarball compatibility. Removing source/types/default/publish maps, changing package names or moving exports is breaking unless old names continue to resolve. Keep source condition for local internal packages and dist-only actual publish staging; retain packed installed consumer, declaration and browser bundle proof.
- APP-005 — preserve necessary difference — tax request limits, anonymous rate identity, shared work pool and safe logging. `packages/calculators/src/work.layer.ts:9-56` gives each composed isolate eight places/five seconds. Timer cannot stop synchronous CPU; late result is rejected (`:25-33`). No global pool is claimed. Do not copy Common Practice wildcard browser CORS (`apps/api/src/http/handler.layer.ts:46-61`) to the tax API. TaxKit admits exact Website origin and disables native client tracing as containment (`apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:189-204`; RPC live `:68`, server `packages/api/rpc/src/server.ts:10-15`). Operational tracing requires reviewed safe fields, actual browser b3/traceparent preflight and errors, rather than changing CORS alone.
- APP-006 — optional — move app-owned MCP tool contracts into a package only if there is a real second consumer. Common Practice's shared ContentToolHandlers works for remote MCP and browser tools (`packages/mcp/src/handlers.layer.ts:6-16`). TaxKit browser tools deliberately operate the page's existing form/answer state; a plain remote calculate handler is not the same interaction. Preserve UI command coordination. Legacy Durable Object session/expiry stays API-host owned regardless of contract location.
- APP-007 — agreed preservation after Q2 — both Bun and Cloudflare remain supported. Native API Worker has HTTP/RPC/MCP with rate policy; Bun host currently serves retained HTTP composition only (`apps/api/src/server.ts:1-28`, `src/index.ts:1-20`, `package.json` dev/start). Preserve Bun launcher and adapter. Do not present Bun `dev` as native-pair proof. Each host requires its own proved request/response/cancellation adapter; shared package code and calculation/report contracts remain host-independent. No need to copy native Cloudflare-only rate binding into Bun.
- APP-008 — important ownership correction for agreed host independence — Cloudflare edge identity extraction is inside RPC package `packages/api/rpc/src/rate-identity.boundary.ts:11-20` (reads `cf-worker`/`cf-connecting-ip` and trusts only direct edge ingress), though it serves all native transports. Move the actual edge trust decision into an app-owned Cloudflare ingress adapter; keep calculator-owned `CalculatorClientRateKey`/`CalculatorRequestRateKey`/`CalculatorAdmission` contracts (`packages/calculators/src/admission.service.ts:10-26`) host-neutral. Preserve old private RPC export as a re-export if current callers need it until imports move. No removal of the trusted private Website calculation method is implied. `apps/api/src/worker-admission.layer.ts:6-59` correctly owns native Alchemy RateLimit construction and adapts it into the calculator interface. `packages/api/rpc/src/host-telemetry.ts:1-27` imports only Effect and is not a Cloudflare runtime coupling; its naming/placement can be reviewed with observability ownership, but do not invent a provider-import violation.

## Shared composition for the agreed Bun and Cloudflare hosts

Direct source search found no imports of Alchemy, `cloudflare:workers`, `@effect/platform-bun`, `@effect/platform-node`, Bun/Node built-ins or ambient `process`, and no `Effect.run*`/ManagedRuntime in current calculator/Core/HTTP/RPC source. The two observed Worker mentions in RPC are explanatory comments, except the concrete edge-header policy listed in APP-008. SDK's private Promise bridge is deliberately an execution boundary; it is not a domain service runner.

Recommended shared composition remains in the API app: one host-neutral route/application Layer merges HTTP and RPC handler Layers using the supplied calculator/content services; native Worker and Bun adapters each acquire that graph once under their host lifetime, supply their own request/cancellation/response services, and close each request's work. Calculator package owns the reusable eight-place/five-second work decoration, input/output Schemas and tax dispatch. Provider-specific identity and rate-binding adapters stay outside packages. The Website stays a separate client-only app. Native Worker continues its incoming Effect execution; Bun uses `HttpRouter.serve` and one top-level `BunRuntime.runMain`; shared service/domain code never runs a Promise or builds a second ManagedRuntime.

Whether Bun gains RPC/MCP host support is a separate supported-surface decision: preserving both hosts does not itself promise a Cloudflare Durable Object equivalent on Bun. text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: /Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/docs/product-specs/common-practice-foundation-review.md
@@
-The remaining comparison, stable findings, candidate version combinations,
-documentation impact and local validation will be linked here before the next
-round. No proposed correction is accepted for implementation yet.
+No proposed correction is accepted for implementation yet. The structured
+[scope](../documentation-audit/common-practice-foundation/audit-scope.json),
+[findings](../documentation-audit/common-practice-foundation/audit-findings.json)
+and [empty implementation crosswalk](../documentation-audit/common-practice-foundation/accepted-findings.json)
+are the audit owners. The dated inventories account for 795 documentation and
+README paths: 737 readable files and 58 retained binary evidence files. Current,
+affected and contradictory owners receive deeper reading; inventory counts
+alone do not establish semantic correctness.
+
+## Intended base and justified differences
+
+| Area | Reuse from Common Practice and scaffold | TaxKit difference to keep |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Apps | Separate Website and API; one frontend server runner; one React-mounted Atom graph; typed private server calls and checked public browser address | Support both Bun and Cloudflare hosts. Preserve the no-JavaScript tax form and its checked submission data. |
+| Domain | One owner for Schemas, operations, errors and live/test service implementations; transports depend inward | Core, calculators and Australian rule packages are real separate capabilities. Do not replace them with a single generic domain package. |
+| Package layout | Explicit exports and ownership-based files | Keep nested `packages/api/*`, `packages/rules/au/*` and `packages/sdk/typescript` unless a separately evidenced move simplifies ownership. A folder rename alone gives no benefit. |
+| Distribution | Source, declaration, default and actual packed-export checks | TaxKit compiles packages and prepares a dist-only SDK. Common Practice's source-only private packages do not establish distributable-package compatibility. All current TaxKit manifests remain private; no publication is established. |
+| Clients | Native generated clients stay private behind named checked operations | Local calculator/SDK errors must not be widened with network failures. Preserve the existing checked RPC contract; add a checked HTTP contract alongside legacy public helpers. |
+| Requests | Native Worker request execution and request-owned cleanup; no backend Promise runner | Preserve ten-second full RPC reply limit, 2 MiB response cap, five-second calculation work limit, eight calculation places per composed isolate and trusted private rate identity. A timer cannot pre-empt synchronous calculation work. |
+| Tools | Shared command contract, strict lint, format, types, tests, build and unused-code checks | Keep release orchestration, the fixed ten-artifact release train, source/declaration/default export modes, staged packing and clean downstream consumers. Common Practice's smaller app-only command graph is insufficient. |
+| Skills | Refreshed published plugin and local profiles | TaxKit's `docs/skills.md` forbids copied shared instructions. Do not reinstall the scaffold's copied-skill trees. First move any required executable lint asset to a code owner with provenance, then retire duplicate instructions. |
+| Deployment | Native Alchemy stack, same-stage pair, own origin from Worker.URL and other host address from a resource Output | Preserve stable resource/state identities, exact Website Origin admission, stage-specific rate counters, stricter secrets policy and separately reviewed provider operations. Newer Alchemy does not contain every TaxKit fix. |
+
+Common Practice source references: `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts`,
+`apps/web/src/lib/runtime.client.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts`,
+`apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/worker.ts`, `packages/http/src/client.layer.ts`
+and package manifests. Scaffold references: `repo-structure/references/tanstack-effect.md`,
+`repository-contract.md`, `tooling-and-docs.md`, and sibling package contracts.
+These are reference implementations, not current TaxKit runtime proof.
+
+## Important corrections and optional simplification
+
+This view follows the structured register. Stable finding IDs remain unchanged
+when Cooper accepts, rejects or defers a correction.
+
+| ID | Consequence and earliest owner | Proposed correction |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| FINDING-001 | An upgrade can restore swallowed provider errors or break the reciprocal Website/API origin graph. Root versions, patches and native graph own this. | Keep the locked baseline; reject an unpatched drop-in upgrade; qualify each patch and candidate against the actual graph. |
+| FINDING-002 | RPC owns a Cloudflare-specific address trust rule. API/Website host ingress should own it. | Move edge-header interpretation to the Cloudflare adapter and supply checked keys to shared admission contracts. Keep the trusted private channel. |
+| FINDING-003 | The HTTP client exposes its generated client and a generic callback helper. `packages/api/http/src/client` owns the correction. | Add named operations, safe errors, a checked address and whole-reply limits. Keep old exports as compatibility adapters. |
+| FINDING-004 | Current summaries still describe the old docs app, starter Website or pre-merge handoff. The documentation routing/lifecycle owner comes first. | Link to current owners, refresh affected summaries and retain dated history. Do not mark remaining clean-slate tasks complete. |
+| FINDING-005 | Copied shared instructions conflict with latest-plugin routing; lint uses an asset from a retained copy. `docs/skills.md` and `tools/oxlint` own this. | Separate qualified executable rule assets from shared instructions, retain provenance and remove copies only after consumers move. |
+| FINDING-006 | Existing workspace checking covers crossings between `src` trees rather than every public-export boundary. `tools/oxlint/package-rules.ts` owns this. | Adapt the scaffold's manifest-aware checks for nested workspaces and prove root/config/app/package cases through the actual lint command. |
+| FINDING-007, optional | Handwritten private Website transports add lifetime and conversion code. Website binding and API host adapters own this. | Prefer native Alchemy Bridge where equivalent trust, cancellation and response consumption are proved. HTTP/RPC choice remains open. |
+
+Declared non-defects: exported telemetry and PostHog are intentionally deferred;
+the placeholder UI package need not become a runtime package; a Bun host need
+not have Cloudflare-specific services; compiled packages and tax-specific limits
+are justified differences. No new generic helpers, duplicate docs renderer or
+second permanent audit system is proposed.
+
+## Complete call paths
+
+**Browser calculation.** The page container mounts the existing Atom command.
+The checked public address supplies a scoped native RPC client. It encodes
+revision-four inputs, reads and decodes the complete bounded reply and releases
+the receive loop. The API RPC handler calls `PublicCalculatorService`; the
+catalogue checks facts and supplies the selected Australian rule/scenario layers
+to Core. Core returns a report and calculation diagnostics. The reply reaches
+the same Atom state, and the leaf renders readonly values. Editing/unmounting
+interrupts pending browser work. Owners: `apps/web/src/lib/calculator-page.container.tsx`,
+`calculator.atoms.ts`, `packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts`,
+`packages/calculators/src/catalog.ts` and `packages/core/src/engine/live.layer.ts`.
+
+**Server form.** Website `src/server.ts` bounds and checks the POST and calls its
+server service. The private binding-only `calculatorRequest` sends the checked
+original connection identity separately from JSON. The API buffers the reply
+before its native method scope ends. Website encodes checked success/failure as
+plain submission data for the page. This supports the no-JavaScript form without
+a second engine. Current private `toRpcAsync` cannot carry an AbortSignal:
+cancellation stops waiting locally, while remote work remains bounded. Do not
+claim immediate remote cancellation. Owners: Website `lib/live.server.layer.ts`
+and API `worker.application.ts`.
+
+**HTTP machine caller.** HTTP API declarations decode the URL, query and body
+with calculator-owned Schemas. The handler calls the same service and preserves
+the current HTTP status/error envelope. Streamed ingress is capped at 64 KiB
+within five seconds. The generated client shares those declarations, but its
+existing public helper has no owned complete-read deadline or response-byte
+policy. That is FINDING-003, not a reason to change tax calculations. Owners:
+`packages/api/http/src/groups/calculators.ts`, `handlers/calculators.ts`,
+`request-boundary.ts` and `client/*`.
+
+**Local SDK.** This is an in-process library, not an HTTP SDK. The caller chooses
+a typed calculator descriptor, the SDK constructs checked request values and

# TaxKit infrastructure foundation: read-only evidence

Reviewed 10 October 2026. TaxKit source: `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit`, commit `f899c963f463d2283517e908febcfa3ebb1dd442`. Common Practice source: `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice`, commit `54a62a5d64892ee2304260f51ef683fb299deea7`.

This work read source, manifests, lockfiles, installed package source/types and official release/registry information. It ran three existing TaxKit provider tests in temporary fixtures with a mocked HTTP client. No real provider commands, deployments, secret reads/changes or registry writes ran. Common Practice stayed clean. The parent agent restored TaxKit's exact committed dependency graph; that was an install of the existing lockfile, not an upgrade. Parent-owned design documents may now be dirty; this subtask did not change project files.

## What can be carried across

Keep the two hosts. The shared packages describe what the application needs; each app supplies the services for its host. Bun supplies the HTTP server and local configuration. Cloudflare supplies the Worker request, private API binding and host-specific rate limit. Shared calculation, API and service contracts need no Alchemy or Cloudflare types.

Common Practice's native Cloudflare logs/traces, checked request categories and stage-owned Worker pair are useful examples. Copy the ownership pattern, not its Site-owned datasets, production monitoring addresses, raw JSON logger or permissive hosted `.env` override.

## Version choices and actual results

| Combination | Evidence | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TaxKit locked Effect ecosystem 4.0.0 + Alchemy beta.80 + committed Alchemy/Atom patches | Current manifest/lock and refreshed installed source. Three mocked redirect tests pass. Parent owns full local qualification. | Current baseline; preserve exact graph until a deliberate candidate is checked. |
| Common Practice/scaffold Effect ecosystem 4.0.2 + unpatched Alchemy beta.81 | Current CP manifest/lock/source; plugin snapshot names this combination. Same TaxKit redirect fixture has 2 passes and 1 failure; forbidden read returns success and writes a replacement ruleset. | Rejected as an unchanged TaxKit upgrade. CP/scaffold success does not qualify TaxKit's graph or rules safety. |
| Effect 4.0.2 + beta.81 with equivalent narrow TaxKit fixes | Peer ranges permit it. Both existing Alchemy fixes still need preservation/adaptation. Whole candidate not installed or qualified here. | A possible next candidate, not an approved upgrade. |
| Effect 4.0.2 + beta.80 with current patches | Alchemy peer ranges permit stable 4.x. Whole candidate not installed or qualified here. | Unqualified alternative. |
| Effect 4.0.0-rc.118 + beta.80/beta.81 | Alchemy peers are `^4.0.0`; this does not admit pre-release rc.118 as an unchanged stable combination. | Not a drop-in candidate. |

The initial TaxKit `node_modules` was stale (Effect rc.117/Alchemy beta.79) while the manifest/lock requested stable 4.0.0/beta.80. The parent then installed the frozen committed graph using Bun 1.4.2; the inspected TaxKit source now matches stable 4.0.0/beta.80. Do not present the stale install as current dependency policy.

Official npm metadata records Effect 4.0.2 published 7 October 2026, Alchemy beta.81 published 5 October 2026. Effect's `rc` and Alchemy's `next` tags are older channels. Tag names and peer compatibility do not prove this application works.

Sources: [Effect registry](https://registry.npmjs.org/effect), [Alchemy registry](https://registry.npmjs.org/alchemy), [Effect release](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/releases/tag/effect%404.0.2), [Alchemy release](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/releases/tag/v2.0.0-beta.81). Safe metadata saved at `/private/tmp/taxkit-infra-registry-research.json`.

### Retained patch evidence

1. Redirect safety: upstream beta.81 still uses `Effect.catch(() => Effect.succeed(undefined))` for every shared redirect-rules read failure. An authorisation failure can be treated as an absent ruleset, followed by replacement. Exact source: `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-alchemy-beta81/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Workers/WorkerProvider.ts:1551`. TaxKit's beta.80 patch catches only `RulesetNotFound`. Owner: `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/patches/alchemy@2.0.0-beta.80.patch`; behavioural test owner `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/packages/infrastructure/src/native-domains-provider.boundary.test.ts:369`.

   Actual temporary test results: `/private/tmp/taxkit-beta80-rule-probe/summary.json` (3 passed), `/private/tmp/taxkit-beta81-rule-probe/summary.json` (2 passed, 1 failed). A verbose beta.81 run printed the safe fixture result `scenario=forbidden, success=true, ruleReads=1, ruleWrites=1`. All calls were mocked. Passing absent/existing cases do not excuse the forbidden case.

2. Reciprocal Worker graph: upstream beta.81 resolves resource properties before checking whether a resource has stable state; `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-alchemy-beta81/packages/alchemy/src/Plan.ts:762`. Patched TaxKit source first keeps fresh, creating or cycle-member resources deferred; `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/node_modules/alchemy/src/Plan.ts:840`. TaxKit deliberately has Website-to-API and API-to-Website references for private binding, output addresses and checked Website-origin policy. Common Practice's simpler one-way binding does not prove this graph works. This subtask compared source; the parent owns graph fixture results.

3. Atom React: both atom-react 4.0.0 and 4.0.2 declare scheduler `>=0.25.0 <0.28.0`, while React 19.3.0 resolves scheduler 0.28.0. TaxKit's patch `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/patches/@effect%2Fatom-react@4.0.0.patch` widens only package peer metadata. It is not an Atom implementation fix. The Commonplace snapshot itself records the mismatch and requires source/declaration, clean consumer, type/build/test and lifecycle checks. Do not silently carry a patch keyed to 4.0.0 into 4.0.2, or claim leaving it unpatched proves browser lifecycle behaviour.

4. Companion versions: platform-bun/platform-node 4.0.2 require node-shared ^4.0.2, and Effect companion packages peer on effect ^4.0.2. TaxKit's explicit node-shared 4.0.0 override would also need intentional review in an aligned 4.0.2 candidate.

Common Practice's Effect 4.0.2 patch changes MCP allowed-origin declarations from a fixed array to an array or predicate; it is unrelated to these TaxKit fixes and should not be copied as an assumed platform requirement.

## Commonplace policy and matching upstream source

The installed and live published Commonplace development-workflows version is 0.6.11. Live release published 8 October 2026. Its 8 October scaffold snapshot names Effect 4.0.2/Alchemy beta.81. The snapshot is a scaffold qualification claim, not fresh TaxKit or provider proof.

Read policy owners under `/Users/cooper/.codex/plugins/cache/commonplace/development-workflows/0.6.11/skills/repo-structure/references/`, including `version-policy.md`, plus `skills/repo-structure/assets/version-snapshot.json`, and Alchemy/hosted-telemetry/native-migration guidance under the same plugin.

Live owners: [plugin manifest](https://github.com/crcorbett/commonplace-plugins/blob/main/plugins/development-workflows/.claude-plugin/plugin.json), [0.6.11 release](https://github.com/crcorbett/commonplace-plugins/releases/tag/%40commonplace/development-workflows%400.6.11).

The existing Effect checkout at `/Users/cooper/Projects/effect` is old v3 source and was left untouched. Matching clean temporary clones:

- Effect tag `effect@4.0.2`, commit `269a7c864351231d42e6e95b7fa8f32050df3691`, `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-effect-4.0.2`.
- Alchemy tag `v2.0.0-beta.81`, commit `e73c66857553a5abe045e1a66b5512cf7d39ef2e`, `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-alchemy-beta81`.

The receiving installed TaxKit 4.0.0/beta.80 types were checked after its frozen install. New upstream source is reference material, not authority to upgrade.

## Axiom resources are different from enabled collection

Common Practice's Axiom stack owns a retained ingest token and five retained dashboards. Another project, Site, owns the physical logs, traces and metrics datasets. The token permits metrics ingestion, but that permission does not mean a metric writer exists. Current code intentionally has no request latency metric and no active custom metrics pipeline.

Exact owners:

- `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/packages/infrastructure/src/axiom/resources.ts:10`: Site ownership, retained token and old token generations requiring deliberate revocation.
- Same file `:20`: token capabilities for all three datasets; `:30`: five dashboards.
- `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/packages/infrastructure/src/axiom/dashboards/types.ts:6`: dataset identity contract; `.../index.ts:8`: dashboard list.
- `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/packages/infrastructure/src/runtime/request-observation.ts:30`: deliberate absence of request latency metric; Worker clocks and histogram series cost.
- `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/packages/infrastructure/src/cloudflare/traces.ts:19`: production token and Site trace dataset references; `:46`: equivalent log destination. Native destinations carry credentials; applications do not need uploader secrets.
- `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/packages/infrastructure/src/stacks/addresses.ts:6`: central production stack addresses; `.../trace-export.ts:17`: hosted stages read the same production destination outputs.

Common Practice Worker declarations enable native invocation logs, traces, sampling 1, persistence and those destinations: `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/apps/web/src/lib/build/cloudflare.ts:81`, `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/worker.ts:60`. API host composition uses native Cloudflare Telemetry plus JSON logging at the latter file `:109`; Website supplies one server runtime at `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts:80`.

Checked application observations are once per response ready, and leave its body stream untouched: `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/packages/infrastructure/src/runtime/request-observation.ts:63`. They capture fixed route family, checked stage and host/isolate fields; this does not prove the visitor received the complete stream. Dashboard stage labels select views, not access rights. `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/packages/infrastructure/src/axiom/dashboards/queries.ts:26` supports this distinction; native root duration includes background waitUntil work.

Cloudflare's official export documentation currently supports logs and traces, and explicitly says infrastructure/custom metrics cannot be exported through this route. Use native Cloudflare metrics for requests, errors, CPU and wall time; wall time includes background work and is not exact visitor latency. Alchemy's Axiom guide and destination type mention an `opentelemetry-metrics` option, but that is not proof Cloudflare supports it. Do not copy that option as a working metrics exporter.

Primary provider sources: [native OpenTelemetry export](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/opentelemetry-export/), [export setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/observability/export/opentelemetry/), [built-in metrics](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/metrics-and-analytics/), [Worker clock](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/performance/). Incorrectly optimistic upstream guide: `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-alchemy-beta81/website/src/content/docs/cloudflare/observability/axiom-observability.mdx:162`; destination type `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-alchemy-beta81/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Workers/ObservabilityDestination.ts:20`.

For TaxKit, platform logs/traces are deliberately disabled: `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/apps/api/src/worker.ts:23`, `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/packages/infrastructure/src/apps-stack.ts:59`. The current fixed-field logger and error reporter discard arbitrary messages, Causes, annotations and span labels: `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/packages/api/rpc/src/host-telemetry.ts:3`. Preserve this privacy floor. Common Practice's `Logger.consoleJson` is not safe to copy unchanged into tax calculation requests. Platform records can contain request URLs separately from application logging; a safe application event contract alone does not qualify platform export.

New TaxKit monitoring should be TaxKit-owned, declared once through native resources and supplied through host composition. There is no evidence TaxKit should depend on Site/Common Practice production stack names or datasets. PostHog is a separate product-data decision and need not be enabled for this operational work.

## Stage and secret differences

Both projects derive their API address from the exact stage's Worker output and bind the Website to that stage's API. Common Practice has independently destroyable Preview Worker pairs and retains Production Workers. Exact owners: `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/apps/web/src/lib/build/cloudflare.ts:192`, `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/packages/infrastructure/src/cloudflare/zone.ts:83`. Preview is a separate named Worker, not a version of the Production Worker. It can use shared Production monitoring destinations, so application separation does not imply monitoring-data separation.

TaxKit's current stage decoder accepts prod / pr-N / dev_identity before Doppler selection: `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/packages/infrastructure/src/apps-secrets.boundary.ts:9`. It maps to taxkit/dev, taxkit/stg_preview or taxkit/prd and disables ambient shell application values `:70`. It has no DotEnv source. Current stage ownership is imported from the retained old Docs deployment owner at `:7`; move the current stage contract to its current owner while preserving accepted values, stack/resource names and historical state identity.

Common Practice centrally uses Doppler, then ignored `.env` override, then disabled process-env fallback: `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/packages/infrastructure/src/secrets.ts:5`. The override applies to local and hosted execution, including empty values. TaxKit's stricter custody is intentional. Keep the current hosted rule; if local `.env` is desired, ask for a local-only choice and test that it cannot override hosted deployment values. Provider authentication remains separate from application-secret selection in both projects.

TaxKit has a deliberately separate local stack/state and local-only rate limit namespace: `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/alchemy.apps.local.run.ts:9`. Preserve the isolated local runner. TaxKit's stage-specific declared namespace strings do not themselves reserve a provider namespace; fresh provider inventory is required before a later apply.

The ready monitoring choice is whether Preview and Production share a TaxKit-owned destination/dataset or own separate ones. Stage filters are useful reports, not a security boundary. Pick separate resources where differing access/privacy/retention is needed. A single checked configuration owner can declare either choice without duplicated application constants. No collection has been enabled by this review.

## Shared services with Bun and Cloudflare

Supported upstream pattern: the host supplies services to shared HTTP routes. Do not put provider/build code in the domain or HTTP contracts.

TaxKit examples:

- `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/packages/api/http/src/server/live.layer.ts:17`: shared HttpApiBuilder/route layer needs services. `:41` currently supplies a particular standalone policy; host behaviour parity must be reviewed, not assumed.
- `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/apps/api/src/server.ts:9`: BunHttpServer supplies the Bun host. `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/apps/api/src/index.ts:1` owns execution.
- `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:86`: Cloudflare host owns composition once, then native request handling. Its exact Website-origin policy is `:201`.
- `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/apps/api/src/worker-admission.layer.ts:1`: Cloudflare rate-limit implementation of the shared admission service. `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/packages/calculators/src/admission.layer.ts:10`: calculator uses the service, without provider imports.
- `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts:10`: one managed Website runtime supplies clients/configuration/safe reporting.

Matching upstream evidence:

- Effect `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-effect-4.0.2/packages/effect/src/http-api/HttpApiBuilder.ts:59` registers shared routes; `:130` captures services without request scope.
- Effect `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-effect-4.0.2/packages/effect/src/http/HttpRouter.ts:592` builds the application layer once and handles the current request/scope. `:1273` serving needs an abstract HttpServer.
- Effect `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-effect-4.0.2/packages/platform/bun/src/BunHttpServer.ts:313` supplies that HTTP server through Bun.
- Alchemy `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-alchemy-beta81/packages/alchemy/src/Http.ts:15` uses the standard Effect HTTP response/request contract. `:21` transfers response/stream scope to its consumer.
- Alchemy `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-alchemy-beta81/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Workers/WorkerBridge.ts:65` supplies request scope, Worker execution context and runtime services; closes non-stream requests through waitUntil. `:243` says the isolate scope has no guaranteed closing hook. `:303` builds/pins the handler once and resets a failed cold-start promise.
- Alchemy `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-alchemy-beta81/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Bridge.ts:1` is a runtime-only entry. The provider/build tooling belongs to deployment composition.
- Alchemy `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-alchemy-beta81/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Workers/Worker.ts:1316` supplies Worker.URL from the native host context, avoiding a separate guessed address.

Official repository links: [Effect shared router](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.2/packages/effect/src/http/HttpRouter.ts), [Effect HTTP API builder](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.2/packages/effect/src/http-api/HttpApiBuilder.ts), [Bun server](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.2/packages/platform/bun/src/BunHttpServer.ts), [Alchemy Worker bridge](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/v2.0.0-beta.81/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Workers/WorkerBridge.ts), [Alchemy runtime bridge](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/v2.0.0-beta.81/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Bridge.ts).

The proposed approach supports shared routes/services and separate host adapters. It does not prove Bun and Worker currently expose identical HTTP/RPC contracts, errors, limits, rate policy or cancellation behaviour; those are implementation/test questions owned by the parent review.

## Native cleanup and rollback limits

Common Practice's dated native-cleanup evidence was gathered on beta.79/Effect rc.117. It reports explicitly approved removal of two retired direct uploader bindings, worker readback, native destinations enabled, a no-op plan and bounded Axiom queries. It is historical hosted proof, not current beta.81/4.0.2 hosted proof: `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/docs/evidence/observability/2026-10-06-native-cleanup.md:8`, `:60`, `:81`. Counts were 119 Website/514 API logs and 120 Website/332 API root spans in its chosen query window; a limit-1000 query is not an exhaustive export or proof of every parent relationship. No uploader secret in code is not proof an old token was revoked.

The older ADR `docs/adr/0001-production-owned-observability.md:3` says the design avoids a third deployment stack, while current source has separate Axiom and export stacks. Follow current source plus the dated evidence, not that stale sentence.

Alchemy `retain` prevents a provider delete while dropping the managed state row. Exact source: `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-alchemy-beta81/packages/alchemy/src/RemovalPolicy.ts:5`. It does not preserve a rollback snapshot. CP Production Worker retention therefore differs from TaxKit's current Worker deletion policy and cannot be adopted by assumption.

TaxKit retains Production zone/DNS ownership but Preview has no zone/domain declaration: `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/packages/infrastructure/src/apps-stack.ts:109`. Its old Docs entrypoint is a retirement marker and retained resource history; do not point it at a new stack name and assume authority/state follows. Restore reviewed source, lockfile and patches locally; any later hosted rollback needs the exact approved artifact/source, old resource identities and provider readback. Existing authority and rollback owners are `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/docs/runbooks/docs-deployment.md:200`, `:242` and `docs/operations/authority-model.md`.

## Ready decisions and next proof

1. Keep both hosts, already agreed. Let each host supply services; keep provider names/types outside shared contracts.
2. Keep the current dependency baseline for this review. Later choose one exact aligned candidate and retain/adapt both Alchemy fixes, plus decide the Atom peer mismatch treatment. No upgrade is authorised now.
3. Preserve TaxKit's safe logging. The safe operational field decision already agreed by the user must have checked schemas and explicit host composition. Choose TaxKit-owned Preview/Production monitoring separation and sampling/persistence before any collection is enabled.
4. Keep hosted Doppler custody and isolated local composition. Optional local-only `.env` override is a separate small choice; do not inherit Common Practice's hosted override.
5. Move the accepted current stage schema away from the old Docs deployment file without changing stage values, physical names or stored identities.
6. Keep cleanup as a named separate operation. Confirm actual native removal support, classify the exact plan and read back old bindings/resources/tokens before claiming retirement. Retained resources and historical evidence remain explicit owners.

Later implementation proof should run in order: source/version/patch review; pure package and packed-consumer tests; mocked create/no-op/update graph plus forbidden-read no-PUT fixtures; Bun and Worker HTTP/error/cancellation/stream checks; emitted Worker and browser checks; exact approved Preview plan/apply/readback and observed safe records; then separately approved Production work with exact rollback identity. Passing local checks is not a deployment receipt.

## Paths read

# TaxKit repository guide

TaxKit is the public monorepo for the open-source tax engine, API, SDK, and
documentation site. Start with [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md), the sole
maintainer-document lifecycle and truth-layer router. `CLAUDE.md` points to this
file; edit `AGENTS.md` only.

## Operating loop

1. Read `docs/README.md`, then only the semantic owner for the task.
2. Confirm the claim against code, configuration, Schemas, exports, generated
   owners, or external readback at the boundary it describes.
3. Put current implementation intent in a SPEC/task and active execution plan;
   never reopen completed work as policy.
4. Update the earliest durable owner and required pointers in the same slice.
5. Run `bun run check:docs`, `bun run check:runbooks` when operations changed,
   focused checks, and `bun run verification`;
   package-facing changes also need an appropriate Changeset.
6. Retain artifact identity, authority, postconditions, limitations,
   non-claims, and rollback.

For any material calculator/rule/schema, SDK/export/example, HTTP/OpenAPI,
public MDX/navigation/runtime, package/app, command/CI/versioning/release-proof,
lifecycle, SPEC, plan, runbook, or skill change, invoke the plugin
`development-workflows:docs-maintainer` route before accepting the slice. Record `Change required`,
`Preserve`, or evidenced `N/A` for its documentation impact. Scheduled or
background freshness work is report-only candidate output unless a separately
attached implementation authority names the reviewer and publisher.

## Task routes

  [`docs/architecture/README.md`](docs/architecture/README.md), then
  [`docs/architecture/package-ownership.md`](docs/architecture/package-ownership.md).

## Engineering guardrails

- Use Effect-native Schema, branded identities, Config, services, Layers,
  tagged errors, collections, Command, and runtime primitives when they own the
  semantics. Decode unknown/representation ingress once and encode egress at
  explicit boundaries.
- Reuse owning Schemas and schema-derived types. Do not mirror raw `id: string`,
  DTOs, provider types, primitive semantic config, or unchecked SDK output.
- Keep primary Effects flat, sequential, and pipe-first where that clarifies
  data flow. Keep one-use mapping/decoding/error logic inline; reject
  helper/common/utils sprawl and generic SDK callback wrappers.
- Keep service contracts, live Layers, test Layers, and executable composition
  separate. Do not run Effects or build live Layers inside domain logic.
- Provider clients expose named Effect operations, `Config.schema` with
  redacted secrets, immediate Schema decoding, safe tagged errors without
  `instanceof`, and live/mock Layers.
- React composition flows route → policy-owning container → focused leaf.
  Routes own transport restoration/outcome matching, containers own commands
  and coordination, and leaves render readonly values/local interaction state.
- Admit an abstraction only with semantic weight, an owner, a real reuse or
  substitution point, a simpler call graph, and focused proof.

## Authority and proof

Tool access is capability, not authority. Provider, registry, publication,
release, deployment, credential, and destructive operations require a named
principal, operation, resource, environment, approval boundary, receipt,
rollback/revocation, and readback. Local gates do not prove publication,
production, or external consumer behavior.

`bun run verification` for repository closeout. Use `bun run release:check`
only for its documented local release-evidence graph; it does not authorize or
prove publication.

Current TaxKit already has the main split: the website calls a separate API, and HTTP, RPC and MCP share the calculation service. The review can focus on bringing that existing work onto the intended base while keeping the tax engine and package contracts.

The installed dependencies still belong to the older checkout. I’ll restore the versions in the committed lockfile before running local checks.

The working shape is:

```text
Website ──┐
HTTP/RPC ─┼─> API ─> calculation service ─> tax rules and engine
MCP ──────┘
SDK ──────────────> calculation service ─> tax rules and engine

Alchemy connects each Website to its own stage’s API.
```

I’d reuse the app connection and request cleanup first, then improve shared clients, qualify dependency versions, and simplify tooling. TaxKit’s tax packages and checked release process need to stay.

One useful difference has emerged: RPC already checks errors and limits how long a call can take. The public HTTP client exposes a lower-level generated client. That needs a safer named client layer while preserving existing exports.
I’ll leave the website transport choice open until the full comparison is ready. The proposal will show the effect of each choice, including whether it changes caller checks, errors or cancellation.

I’ll record that both Bun and Cloudflare stay, and that shared packages must work without knowing which host runs them. I’ll check the upstream Effect server layers and Alchemy’s Worker setup to show exactly where each host supplies its needs.

The version review also found that newer Alchemy `beta.81` still lacks two fixes TaxKit currently carries. Moving to the newer release will need to retain or replace those fixes and prove the result locally.

I’ve recorded both settled choices in decision records: support both hosts, and keep financial values out of operational observations. The calculation glossary now distinguishes a calculation trace from an operational record.

The initial documentation check passed. Full local verification is running; I’ll report its result separately from the design findings and deployed behaviour.

The first full check stopped while building a controlled website failure case. It reported that the build child exited, but did not give a clear cause. I’ll keep that as a failed check and retry the affected local build with the permissions it needs.

Separately, a compatibility test reproduced a real issue in unpatched Alchemy `beta.81`: it treats a forbidden provider read as success. That confirms TaxKit’s existing patch cannot simply be dropped.

The focused tax checks passed: 162 tests across the engine, calculators and Australian rule packages. They cover the existing checked cases; they do not prove every possible tax situation.

The comparison also supports keeping TaxKit’s compiled packages and packed-SDK checks. Common Practice’s private packages run directly from TypeScript source. Copying that package setup into TaxKit would weaken the checks used for distributable packages.

# TaxKit repository guide

TaxKit is the public monorepo for the open-source tax engine, API, SDK, and
documentation site. Start with [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md), the sole
maintainer-document lifecycle and truth-layer router. `CLAUDE.md` points to this
file; edit `AGENTS.md` only.

## Operating loop

1. Read `docs/README.md`, then only the semantic owner for the task.
2. Confirm the claim against code, configuration, Schemas, exports, generated
   owners, or external readback at the boundary it describes.
3. Put current implementation intent in a SPEC/task and active execution plan;
   never reopen completed work as policy.
4. Update the earliest durable owner and required pointers in the same slice.
5. Run `bun run check:docs`, `bun run check:runbooks` when operations changed,
   focused checks, and `bun run verification`;
   package-facing changes also need an appropriate Changeset.
6. Retain artifact identity, authority, postconditions, limitations,
   non-claims, and rollback.

For any material calculator/rule/schema, SDK/export/example, HTTP/OpenAPI,
public MDX/navigation/runtime, package/app, command/CI/versioning/release-proof,
lifecycle, SPEC, plan, runbook, or skill change, invoke the plugin
`development-workflows:docs-maintainer` route before accepting the slice. Record `Change required`,
`Preserve`, or evidenced `N/A` for its documentation impact. Scheduled or
background freshness work is report-only candidate output unless a separately
attached implementation authority names the reviewer and publisher.

## Task routes

- Repository and package topology:
  [`docs/architecture/README.md`](docs/architecture/README.md), then
  [`docs/architecture/package-ownership.md`](docs/architecture/package-ownership.md).
- Effect services and boundaries:
  [`docs/architecture/effect-services.md`](docs/architecture/effect-services.md)
  and the applicable package README.
- API/SDK: [`docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md`](docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md),
  [`apps/api/README.md`](apps/api/README.md), and
  [`packages/sdk/typescript/README.md`](packages/sdk/typescript/README.md).
- Calculators/rules/facts: the focused owner under `docs/architecture/` and the
  owning package README.
- Frontend/public docs:
  [`docs/architecture/frontend.md`](docs/architecture/frontend.md),
  [`docs/architecture/content-and-posts.md`](docs/architecture/content-and-posts.md),
  and [`apps/docs/README.md`](apps/docs/README.md).
- Current work: [`docs/product-specs/index.md`](docs/product-specs/index.md) and
  [`docs/exec-plans/active/README.md`](docs/exec-plans/active/README.md).
- Standards, tests, and release checks:
  [`docs/standards/README.md`](docs/standards/README.md) and
  [`docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md`](docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md).
- Repeatable release, versioning, packed-consumer and recovery operations:
  [`docs/runbooks/README.md`](docs/runbooks/README.md) and
  [`docs/operations/authority-model.md`](docs/operations/authority-model.md).
- References and audits: [`docs/references/README.md`](docs/references/README.md)
  and [`docs/documentation-audit/README.md`](docs/documentation-audit/README.md).

## Engineering guardrails

- Use Effect-native Schema, branded identities, Config, services, Layers,
  tagged errors, collections, Command, and runtime primitives when they own the
  semantics. Decode unknown/representation ingress once and encode egress at
  explicit boundaries.
- Reuse owning Schemas and schema-derived types. Do not mirror raw `id: string`,
  DTOs, provider types, primitive semantic config, or unchecked SDK output.
- Keep primary Effects flat, sequential, and pipe-first where that clarifies
  data flow. Keep one-use mapping/decoding/error logic inline; reject
  helper/common/utils sprawl and generic SDK callback wrappers.
- Keep service contracts, live Layers, test Layers, and executable composition
  separate. Do not run Effects or build live Layers inside domain logic.
- Provider clients expose named Effect operations, `Config.schema` with
  redacted secrets, immediate Schema decoding, safe tagged errors without
  `instanceof`, and live/mock Layers.
- React composition flows route → policy-owning container → focused leaf.
  Routes own transport restoration/outcome matching, containers own commands
  and coordination, and leaves render readonly values/local interaction state.
- Admit an abstraction only with semantic weight, an owner, a real reuse or
  substitution point, a simpler call graph, and focused proof.

## Authority and proof

Tool access is capability, not authority. Provider, registry, publication,
release, deployment, credential, and destructive operations require a named
principal, operation, resource, environment, approval boundary, receipt,
rollback/revocation, and readback. Local gates do not prove publication,
production, or external consumer behavior.

Use `bun run check:repository-paths` for checkout portability and
`bun run verification` for repository closeout. Use `bun run release:check`
only for its documented local release-evidence graph; it does not authorize or
prove publication.

## Shared development skills

Before starting work, follow [the plugin lookup](docs/skills.md) and load the
latest published Commonplace `development-workflows` plugin. Do not use saved
repository copies or assume a cached plugin version is current. Read the local
profiles in `docs/skill-profiles/` alongside the plugin.

# Common Practice foundation review plan

This plan executes the authorised investigation and design discussion in the
[review proposal](../../product-specs/common-practice-foundation-review.md).
It does not authorise implementation. The earlier clean-slate plan remains
active and retains its task and proof owners.

1. Establish exact checkouts, refreshed published skills and preserved work.
2. Account for documentation, configuration and representative code; trace
   website, HTTP, RPC, MCP and SDK calls through the shared tax service.
3. Compare host independence, package exports, native request cleanup,
   dependency versions, Alchemy stage wiring, Doppler and safe observations.
4. Publish a local candidate audit, findings and migration sequence. Run local
   checks and obtain a fresh independent review.
5. Interview Cooper in dependency order. Record agreed terms and meaningful
   trade-offs as answers arrive. Keep unresolved choices open.
6. Obtain shared understanding and acceptance of finding IDs before mapping
   any accepted correction to implementation requirements and tasks.

Rollback for this design-only slice is to remove its review documents and
restore its exact glossary/index changes while retaining dated failed and
accepted evidence. It changes no runtime or deployed resource. Any later
implementation plan must give each step its own owning paths, compatibility
proof, rollback and separate external authority where needed.

# Common Practice foundation review plan

This plan executes the authorised investigation and design discussion in the
[review proposal](../../product-specs/common-practice-foundation-review.md).
It does not authorise implementation. The earlier clean-slate plan remains
active and retains its task and proof owners.

1. Establish exact checkouts, refreshed published skills and preserved work.
2. Account for documentation, configuration and representative code; trace
   website, HTTP, RPC, MCP and SDK calls through the shared tax service.
3. Compare host independence, package exports, native request cleanup,
   dependency versions, Alchemy stage wiring, Doppler and safe observations.
4. Publish a local candidate audit, findings and migration sequence. Run local
   checks and obtain a fresh independent review.
5. Interview Cooper in dependency order. Record agreed terms and meaningful
   trade-offs as answers arrive. Keep unresolved choices open.
6. Obtain shared understanding and acceptance of finding IDs before mapping
   any accepted correction to implementation requirements and tasks.

Rollback for this design-only slice is to remove its review documents and
restore its exact glossary/index changes while retaining dated failed and
accepted evidence. It changes no runtime or deployed resource. Any later
implementation plan must give each step its own owning paths, compatibility
proof, rollback and separate external authority where needed.
